declarations.docstring: The algebra endomorphism of the matrix-coordinate polynomial ring that sends the coordinate matrix to the transpose of a given matrix times the coordinate matrix.
The transpose-multiplication algebra homomorphism sends the coordinate indexed by `(i, j)` to the sum of `M (l, i)` times the coordinates indexed by `(l, j)`.
The transpose-multiplication polynomial algebra homomorphism commutes under composition with an auxiliary algebra homomorphism.

The transpose-multiplication polynomial algebra homomorphism maps the determinant of the coordinate matrix to the product of the constant polynomial associated with the matrix determinant and the coordinate-matrix determinant.
The transpose-multiplication polynomial algebra homomorphism preserves membership in the ideal generated by the determinant of the coordinate matrix.
The polynomial algebra homomorphism associated with a product of matrices is the composition of the associated homomorphisms.
The polynomial algebra homomorphism associated with the identity matrix is the identity.

Applying the transpose-multiplication polynomial algebra homomorphism entrywise to the coordinate matrix yields the coefficientwise constant image of the transposed matrix times the coordinate matrix.
The representation of the general linear group on the matrix-coordinate polynomial ring whose action uses the transpose coefficients of the underlying matrix.
The action of an invertible matrix in the representation is the algebra homomorphism associated with its underlying matrix.
An invertible matrix sends the coordinate indexed by `(i, j)` to the sum of its entries at `(l, i)` times the coordinates indexed by `(l, j)`.
Each endofunction arising from the transpose-coefficient action commutes with the auxiliary endofunction associated with another invertible matrix.
